projects/worldlogic-terrain-1.21.1-neofo.comparison: Compared at 1x, 4x and tiled 3x3 with dark oak: the four-board construction stays recognizable while the hue is charcoal rather than brown. The dark seams are intentional board joints, not gaps in alpha.

findings.silhouette: Four horizontal boards with one-pixel seams and staggered end joints remain legible.
findings.cluster_structure: Rows 1–3 contain long joined midtone groups with shorter adjoining grain shifts.
findings.micro_contrast: The warm charcoal grain changes in small steps within the board faces.
findings.light_and_volume: Upper board edge is lighter than the lower edge, implying a shallow bevel.
findings.material_continuity: All opaque face pixels use a muted brown-grey ramp consistent with finished ebony.
findings.edge_variation: End joints shift from x7 to x12, x3 and x9 across courses.
findings.variant_identity: Ebony retains a dark charcoal face unlike mahogany's muted warm red.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Dark oak uses the same horizontal board scale and broken joint rhythm.
findings.functional_material_cues: Horizontal grain and dark joints distinguish sawn boards from bark.

projects/worldlogic-terrain-1.21.1-neofo.comparison: Compared at native size and 4x with dark oak sapling: a forked woody stem and attached asymmetric leaf groups replace the old simple green cap; the reduced young crown is intentional.

findings.silhouette: A low irregular crown extends to the left and reaches upward on the right.
findings.cluster_structure: The leaf tips at the upper right and lower left connect to shaded leaf bases.
findings.micro_contrast: Olive green tip pixels meet darker neighboring green groups.
findings.light_and_volume: The brown stem has lighter central faces next to the darker turning branches.
findings.material_continuity: Green foliage stays attached to the warm brown wood, with no arbitrary accent flecks.
findings.edge_variation: Uneven branch lengths and open space between foliage groups avoid a square crown.
findings.variant_identity: The split and leaning ebony leader reads shorter and more asymmetric than mahogany.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Dark oak demonstrates recognizable branch attachments and a small native-scale crown.
findings.branch_hierarchy: The central woody stem divides into two main arms and a small lower left shoot.
findings.species_silhouette: The short spreading side shoots and upright right tip make a squat juvenile.
findings.foliage_attachment: Leaf bases meet the brown branch pixels at the tips rather than float separately.

projects/worldlogic-terrain-1.21.1-neofo.comparison: Compared at 1x, 4x and 3x3 with mangrove planks: horizontal construction is preserved, but the reddish-brown face is less saturated and uses its own joint positions.

findings.silhouette: Four boards remain distinct, each separated by a one-pixel reddish-brown seam.
findings.cluster_structure: Warm contiguous grain areas extend along the upper and middle board rows.
findings.micro_contrast: The small darker groups inside rows 3 and 7 emphasize the grain without speckles.
findings.light_and_volume: A lighter upper rim and restrained lower shadows describe the board edges.
findings.material_continuity: Muted terracotta and brown shades carry through each opaque sawn face.
findings.edge_variation: The joins shift between the middle, left and right of successive boards.
findings.variant_identity: The reddish-brown palette contrasts with ebony's neutral charcoal while keeping the vanilla board motif.

projects/worldlogic-terrain-1.21.1-neofo.comparison: Compared at native size and 4x with jungle sapling: a taller single leader carries offset leaf clusters instead of a solid oval silhouette; the paired side shoots are deliberate.

findings.silhouette: The narrow upright profile rises to a terminal crown above two offset lateral tiers.
findings.cluster_structure: The upper and side clusters contain small adjoining green shade groups.
findings.micro_contrast: Tip greens step into darker greens at the points where leaves meet the twig.
findings.light_and_volume: A lighter brown strip on the lower stem sits beside darker wood pixels.
findings.material_continuity: The restrained leaf and wood ramps distinguish thin young bark and green foliage.
findings.edge_variation: Uneven left and right tier heights break the outer contour.
findings.variant_identity: A straight central leader and staggered branches distinguish it from forked ebony.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Jungle sapling supplies the tall juvenile role and closely scaled stem reference.
findings.branch_hierarchy: A continuous main leader supports smaller side shoots at separate heights.
findings.species_silhouette: An erect single leader with paired leaflets suggests a tropical seedling.
findings.foliage_attachment: Each side cluster connects inward through a darker leaf base to its branch.
